legend.title: How each row of the ring figures is made.
legend.body: Shown for one pair, R DHC – R RSC (comparison 1, gamma coherence; the pair whose change is largest), each bar the mean over the rats. a, the Precon1 cue effect: the cue window's coherence minus the baseline's, on Precon1 (a–c of a ring figure). b, the Precon4 cue effect, the same on Precon4 (d–f). c, the change in cue effect: Precon4's minus Precon1's (g–i), the number tab 8's light tests. Orange arrows: up; purple: down. A ring draws this for every pair at once, each line's width the size of its number.

legend.title: Baseline (20 s) → both cues, theta 5–12 Hz: the connectome of the change from Baseline (20 s) to Cue 1 + Cue 2 (20 s).
legend.body: a–c, the Precon1 cue effect (Cues − Baseline, on Precon1); d–f, the Precon4 cue effect; g–i, the change in cue effect (Precon4’s minus Precon1’s). Each ring holds the 6 regions (open, a region no pair reaches with at least 4 rats); each edge is one of the 15 pairs tested, curving toward the centre, its width the mean change in coherence from Baseline (20 s) to Cue 1 + Cue 2 (20 s) over the rats (Dickson 2022: 59–61 Hz notch, hanning(1024), 512 overlap, 2,048 points, averaged over 30–90 Hz without 59–61 Hz), orange for an increase and purple for a decrease. Left column, the increases; middle, the decreases; right, both. Under each ring, its statistic (the summed increases, the summed decreases, or the sum of all) against 10,000 sets of fake trials from the same rats’ FP1 and FP2 recordings, where there were no cues: a fake cue onset every 10 s of FP, the trial’s own windows round it, measured as a trial’s are; in each set every session gets as many fake trials as it had real ones, drawn at random with replacement, each with its two windows in random order (with no cue, either can stand for it) and losing the windows the matching real trial lost to clipping, and its change is made as the real one is. The vertical line is the observed value, with its rank among the sets and its P (increases one-sided upward, decreases downward, both two-sided; *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001; uncorrected). n = 8 rats, 8 trials per session. Significant: Precon4 cue effect, increases: P < 0.001; Precon4 cue effect, both: P < 0.001; Change in cue effect, increases: P < 0.001; Change in cue effect, both: P < 0.001.

legend.title: Baseline (20 s) → both cues · followed up from the theta coherence of R ACC – R OFC: direction.
legend.body: a, the pair on the ring of regions (the arrow, the direction measured). Then, for each measure: its value for each rat at Baseline (20 s) and Cue 1 + Cue 2 (20 s) on Precon1 (grey) and Precon4 (black), each rat's two windows joined, the mean ± s.e.m. beside them; each rat's change between the days, (Precon4 Cue 1 + Cue 2 (20 s) − Baseline (20 s)) − (Precon1 Cue 1 + Cue 2 (20 s) − Baseline (20 s)), with the mean ± 95% confidence interval; and that mean against 10,000 shuffles in which each session's trials had their two windows swapped at random (grey) and against 10,000 sets of fake trials from the same rats' FP1 and FP2, where there were no cues, each session as many as it had real trials, in random order, losing the windows its real trials lost (blue). The pair was followed up because its own change in coherence had P < 0.05 (uncorrected; no pair survives correction on its own), and of the measures run on it these are the ones whose t-test had P < 0.05: they are leads, chosen by that test. Granger R ACC → R OFC: FP intervals P < 0.001, rank 10,001 of 10,001; within-session shuffles P < 0.001, rank 10,001 of 10,001; t(7) = 11.81, P < 0.001 (one-sample t-test of each rat's change, uncorrected); Granger R OFC → R ACC: FP intervals P < 0.001, rank 10,001 of 10,001; within-session shuffles P < 0.001, rank 10,001 of 10,001; t(7) = 19.57, P < 0.001 (one-sample t-test of each rat's change, uncorrected).

Each ring holds the 6 regions (open, a region no pair reaches with at least 4 rats); each edge is one of the 15 pairs tested, curving toward the centre, its width the mean change in coherence from Baseline (10 s) to Cue 1 over the rats (Dickson 2022: 59–61 Hz notch, hanning(1024), 512 overlap, 2,048 points, averaged over 30–90 Hz without 59–61 Hz), orange for an increase and purple for a decrease. Left column, the increases; middle, the decreases; right, both. Under each ring, its statistic (the summed increases, the summed decreases, or the sum of all) against 10,000 shuffles in which each session’s trials had their two windows swapped at random (the sign of that trial’s change flipped: trial-to-trial noise inside each session), the vertical line the observed value, with its rank among the shuffles and its permutation P (increases one-sided upward, decreases downward, both two-sided; *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001; uncorrected). n = 8 rats, 8 trials per session. Significant: none.

alts.null_why: every way of flipping the sign of each rat’s change, the rat as the unit, as tab 8’s light

Significant: none.

legend.title: Cue 1 → cue 2, theta 5–12 Hz: the connectome of the change from Cue 1 to Cue 2.
legend.body: a–c, the Precon1 cue 1→2 effect (Cue 2 − Cue 1, on Precon1); d–f, the Precon4 cue 1→2 effect; g–i, the change in cue 1→2 effect (Precon4’s minus Precon1’s). Each ring holds the 6 regions (open, a region no pair reaches with at least 4 rats); each edge is one of the 15 pairs tested, curving toward the centre, its width the mean change in coherence from Cue 1 to Cue 2 over the rats (Dickson 2022: 59–61 Hz notch, hanning(1024), 512 overlap, 2,048 points, averaged over 30–90 Hz without 59–61 Hz), orange for an increase and purple for a decrease. Left column, the increases; middle, the decreases; right, both. Under each ring, its statistic (the summed increases, the summed decreases, or the sum of all) against 10,000 sets of fake trials from the same rats’ FP1 and FP2 recordings, where there were no cues: a fake cue onset every 10 s of FP, the trial’s own windows round it, measured as a trial’s are; in each set every session gets as many fake trials as it had real ones, drawn at random with replacement, each with its two windows in random order (with no cue, either can stand for it) and losing the windows the matching real trial lost to clipping, and its change is made as the real one is. The vertical line is the observed value, with its rank among the sets and its P (increases one-sided upward, decreases downward, both two-sided; *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001; uncorrected). n = 8 rats, 8 trials per session. Significant: Precon4 cue 1→2 effect, decreases: P < 0.001; Precon4 cue 1→2 effect, both: P < 0.001; Change in cue 1→2 effect, decreases: P < 0.001; Change in cue 1→2 effect, both: P < 0.001.

legend.title: Cue 1 → cue 2 · followed up from the theta coherence of R ACC – R OFC: direction.
legend.body: a, the pair on the ring of regions (the arrow, the direction measured). Then, for each measure: its value for each rat at Cue 1 and Cue 2 on Precon1 (grey) and Precon4 (black), each rat's two windows joined, the mean ± s.e.m. beside them; each rat's change between the days, (Precon4 Cue 2 − Cue 1) − (Precon1 Cue 2 − Cue 1), with the mean ± 95% confidence interval; and that mean against 10,000 shuffles in which each session's trials had their two windows swapped at random (grey) and against 10,000 sets of fake trials from the same rats' FP1 and FP2, where there were no cues, each session as many as it had real trials, in random order, losing the windows its real trials lost (blue). The pair was followed up because its own change in coherence had P < 0.05 (uncorrected; no pair survives correction on its own), and of the measures run on it these are the ones whose t-test had P < 0.05: they are leads, chosen by that test. Granger R ACC → R OFC: FP intervals P < 0.001, rank 1 of 10,001; within-session shuffles P < 0.001, rank 1 of 10,001; t(7) = −42.97, P < 0.001 (one-sample t-test of each rat's change, uncorrected); Granger R OFC → R ACC: FP intervals P < 0.001, rank 1 of 10,001; within-session shuffles P < 0.001, rank 1 of 10,001; t(7) = −13.67, P < 0.001 (one-sample t-test of each rat's change, uncorrected).
